# dsh-quicktime-player
A sidebar video player for **DeepSeek Harness** — streaming playback with seek, wheel zoom and drag

pan, plus frame
capture and clip export.
## Features
- **Plays from anywhere.** Registers its own right-sidebar tab type, so any video opened through DSH

— Files tab,
chat file reference, another sidebar plugin's tree, `sidebar_open` — lands in this pla

yer. Nothing else needs to be
installed, and no other plugin needs adapting.
- **Seekable.** A Host

route streams bytes with HTTP `Range` (`206`), so the progress bar scrubs instead of snapping
back.

Bytes stay on disk — a multi-GB video is never read into memory.
- **Seek works on Desktop too.** Th

e Electron shell serves the page from `dsh-app://`, where Chromium cannot seek a
`<video>` response;

the player therefore streams from a tokenized `127.0.0.1` port and falls back to the
same-origin ro

ute when that port is unavailable.
- **Zoom and pan.** Wheel zooms around the pointer (1× – 8×), dra

g pans while zoomed, and panning stops at the
video's edge — the picture can never be dragged out of

the frame. Double-click toggles fullscreen.
- **Own controls.** Play/pause, time ⇄ frame number, sp

eed slider (0.2× – 5×, 0.2 steps), loop, vertical volume
popup, mute, picture-in-picture, fullscreen

. The chrome fades out while the mouse is idle.
- **Frame stepping.** ← / → step one frame; the fram

e rate is measured from delivered frames.
- **Picks up where you left off.** Each file's position, s

peed, loop, volume and mute are remembered by absolute path
(the last 50 files, ignored after 30 day

s), so switching sessions and coming back resumes on the same frame. If the
file was re-rendered (du

ration changed), the old record is dropped rather than seeking somewhere unrelated.
- **Copy the cur
rent frame.** The camera button next to `?` writes the frame under the playhead to the clipboard as

a PNG (falling back to a download), with a toast confirming it.
- **Trim a range.** The scissors but

ton drops a marker at the playhead; two markers survive, linked by a dashed line,
and hovering the s

cissors reveals save/clear. Saving runs the Host's `ffmpeg` with a stream copy, so the clip is
byte-
identical to the source — no re-encode, cut on the nearest keyframe. Without `ffmpeg` the button say

s so.
- **Check for updates.** The cloud button next to the camera asks the Host for this package's

installed version and
the registry's latest, then reports the answer in a small dialog. Manual only:

no polling, no badge, no auto-install.
- **Follows the harness theme.** The chrome (header, guide c

ard, dialogs, toasts) is painted with DSH's own
`--dsw-alias-*` tokens, so a light theme gives a lig

ht player; the video stage stays dark because that is what sits
under the picture. Without the token

s it falls back to the dark palette it has always used.
- **Built-in guide.** The `?` in the corner

lays a click-through guide card over the player: one row per feature,
with the same control glyphs y

ou see in the toolbar. It is plain text — no arrows to keep in sync.
- **Keyboard is never stolen.**

While focus is inside the pane — even on a slider — Space and the arrows
stay with the player.

Reopen the window once so the client bundle is picked up.
## Requirements

- DSH with profile bundles (the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`).
- **`ffmpeg` on the Host, only

for clip export.** It is looked up at `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg`,
`/usr/local/bin/ffmpeg`, then `ff

mpeg` on `PATH`. Without it everything else still works; the save button says the
Host has no `ffmpe
g` instead of failing silently.
There is nothing to configure: the route prefix, the 4 GiB ceiling, the loopback media server and th

e working-directory
confinement are fixed.
## Controls
| Input | Action |

| Space / K | play / pause |
| ← → | one frame back / forward |
| Shift + ← → | ±1 s |
| ↑ ↓ | volum

e |
| M | mute |
| F / Enter | fullscreen |
| 0 | reset zoom |
| + / − | zoom in / out |
| click the

clock | switch between time and frame numbers |
| the scissors button | drop a clip marker at the p

layhead (the last two are kept) |
| hover the scissors | reveal save / clear for the marked range |

| the camera button | copy the current frame to the clipboard as a PNG |
| the cloud button | check
the registry for a newer version |
## How it works

- **One tab type.** `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register` claims video addresses with per-suffix globs
(`d
sh-resource://file/**/*.mp4`, …). The registry ranks tab types by band, then by pattern length, then

by
registration order — a longer, video-only glob outranks a sidebar plugin's generic `dsh-resource

://file/**`, so
videos route here and every other file keeps its usual viewer.
- **One Host route.**

`ctx.webServer.register` serves `/quicktime/source`, `/quicktime/stream`, `/quicktime/clip`,
`/quic
ktime/capabilities`, `/quicktime/version` and the tokenized loopback port. Paths are confined to the

session
working directory.
- **Clip export** shells out to `ffmpeg` with `-ss / -t -c copy`: the st

reams are copied, not re-encoded, so the cut
lands on the nearest keyframe and the frame data stays

byte-identical. The temp file is deleted after it is sent.
- No dependency on any other plugin: the
core is the tab type plus that route.
`.mkv`, `.avi`, `.wmv` and `.flv` are accepted but Chromium cannot decode them; the player reports t

hat instead of
pretending to play.
## Troubleshooting
- `~/.dsh/quicktime-player.log` — one JSON line per player event (source resolved, metadata, decode

errors).
- "宿主上没有 ffmpeg" when saving a clip — install `ffmpeg` (`brew install ffmpeg`) and reopen t

he window.
- The update check says "检查失败" — the Host could not reach `registry.npmjs.org` (offline,

proxy, or DNS).
- `GET /quicktime/_graph` — dev probe for whether the client bundle is in the module

or DNS).
- `GET /quicktime/_graph` — dev probe for whether the client bundle is in the module graph.
## License
MIT. The icon is ours: a dark plate, a gradient ring and a play glyph, generated by `scripts/make-ic

on.mjs`
(violet, teal, amber or rose). It contains no Apple artwork.
